_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph
params.convention: The sampling period of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard, 20 Hz (one scene every 50 ms): the step bound of headingSince, the largest gap between two consecutive scenes it integrates across; not a look-back window and not an action window.

params.name: p.conflict_horizon
params.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
params.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987)

params.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
params.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
params.source: passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P: 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

params.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
params.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
params.source: speed noise floor of vehicle odometry and tracked-object estimates

params.name: p.exhibition_accel_min
params.convention: harsh-acceleration threshold: a longitudinal acceleration of about 0.4 g, beyond ordinary driving
params.source: naturalistic driving studies' harsh-event thresholds (e.g. SHRP2, 100-Car study)

params.name: p.exhibition_speed_min
params.convention: a speed of about 100 mph, beyond any posted limit in the jurisdiction
params.source: highest posted limits in Nevada (80 mph) plus a margin

params.name: p.contest_accel_min
params.convention: a sustained acceleration well above ordinary launches (about 0.25 g) held by both vehicles
params.source: naturalistic driving acceleration distributions

params.name: p.contest_window
params.convention: duration a side-by-side hard acceleration must last to be a contest rather than a merge
params.source: drag-race launch durations

params.name: p.contest_same_direction_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 18 degrees) for travel in the same direction
params.source: lane-level heading alignment tolerance

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
params.source: MUTCD 3B.16 (stop line placed 4 ft in advance of a crosswalk) plus driver placement margin

params.name: p.attention_ttc_min
params.convention: time-to-collision threshold of a critical rear-end conflict
params.source: van der Horst (1990) rear-end TTC thresholds

params.name: p.overtake_window
params.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
params.source: AASHTO Green Book passing-manoeuvre model: passing times of about 4 to 11 s

params.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
params.source: heading angles of urban lane changes, typically below 20 degrees

params.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
params.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
params.source: geometric convention separating walking along a roadway from crossing it, from pedestrian heading resolution

params.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
params.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
params.source: pedestrian tracking heading resolution and path deviation observed in square crossings

params.name: p.grade_separation_reach
params.convention: ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a pedestrian tunnel or overpass within which a roadway crossing is made at the point that facility serves: the facility's width plus the stair or ramp landings at either end
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Planning, Design and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities: overpass stairs and ramps landing within about 30 m of the crossing line

params.name: p.blind_person_approach_reach
params.convention: the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

params.name: p.immediate_stop_window
params.convention: the longest time from the moment a stop is due until the road user is at rest for the stop to be immediate: a 1 s perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s at 4.5 m/s^2
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: the longest duration of a turn at a junction by a bicycle or a scooter, from the start of its heading change to its end
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities, turning speeds and radii at intersections

params.name: p.turn_heading_min
params.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
params.source: naturalistic-driving manoeuvre classification by heading-change thresholds

params.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
params.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
params.source: naturalistic-driving manoeuvre classification by heading-change thresholds

params.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
params.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
params.source: inertial and tracking yaw-rate resolution of the acquisition standard

params.name: p.rider_crossing_motion_cos
params.convention: largest absolute cosine between a rider's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the rider counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
params.source: bicycle crossing-trajectory observation at mid-block and intersection crossings

params.name: p.usable_path_width_min
params.convention: the narrowest width of a bicycle path at which one bicycle or scooter rider can operate on it: the essential operating space of a bicyclist
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), bicyclist operating space

params.name: p.bicycle_reaction_time
params.convention: perception-reaction time of a bicyclist in the stopping-sight-distance model
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

params.name: p.bicycle_decel_dry
params.convention: braking deceleration of a bicycle on a dry paved surface in the stopping-sight-distance model (coefficient of friction about 0.32)
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

params.name: p.bicycle_decel_wet
params.convention: braking deceleration of a bicycle on a wet surface in the stopping-sight-distance model (coefficient of friction about 0.16)
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

params.name: p.bicycle_decel_ice
params.convention: braking deceleration on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.05)
params.source: winter road-surface friction measurements

params.name: p.bicycle_lamp_reach
params.convention: the distance ahead a bicycle headlamp lights the path in darkness, within which the rider can see an obstacle
params.source: bicycle headlamp illumination ranges

params.name: p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol
params.convention: the share of a vehicle's speed across the line to the roundabout's centre at or below which its motion counts as towards or away from the centre rather than around it: within about 15 degrees of the radial direction
params.source: roundabout entry and exit path geometry (FHWA Roundabouts: An Informational Guide, NCHRP Report 672)

params.name: p.roundabout_critical_gap
params.convention: critical headway of an entering driver at a single-lane roundabout: the shortest time to the next conflicting road user an entering driver accepts
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual, 6th edition, roundabouts chapter

params.name: p.delivery_halt_min_duration
params.convention: the shortest halt counted as a pick-up or delivery stop en route rather than a halt in traffic: the short end of a goods vehicle's curbside dwell
params.source: urban freight curbside dwell-time studies

params.name: p.queue_halt_gap
params.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
params.source: queue spacing at jam density in traffic flow practice (Highway Capacity Manual)

params.name: p.mail_drop_box_reach
params.convention: the ground distance from a halted vehicle's body to a mail drop box within which a driver can post mail from the vehicle or a step away
params.source: kerbside drop-box placement practice: box set at the curb face, reach of an arm plus one step

params.name: p.mail_deposit_max_halt
params.convention: the longest halt counted as expeditious deposit of mail into a drop box: pull up, post, pull away
params.source: curbside dwell of a single drop-off in curb management studies

params.name: p.standing_min_duration
params.convention: the longest halt counted as receiving or discharging passengers or loading rather than standing: a passenger pick-up dwell at the curb
params.source: curbside passenger pick-up and drop-off dwell times in curb management studies

params.name: p.parked_heading_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about fourteen degrees) between a standing vehicle's heading and its carrier's designated direction at which it counts as parallel with the edge and headed with traffic
params.source: parallel-parking placement tolerance in curb parking practice

params.name: p.parking_min_duration
params.convention: the longest halt counted as temporary, as for loading or unloading: a common time limit of a passenger loading zone
params.source: municipal passenger loading zone time limits

params.name: p.parking_space_angle_resolution
params.convention: the bay angle at or below which a mapped parking bay counts as parallel to the curb rather than angled: the source's angle resolution for mapped bays
params.source: angle resolution of the source's map annotation

params.name: p.curb_parallel_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about fourteen degrees) between a stopped bus's heading and its carrier's designated direction, in either sense, at which the bus counts as approximately parallel to the curb
params.source: transit agency bus stop design guidance on bus alignment at the curb

params.name: p.following_headway_dry
params.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a dry surface: the two-second rule of driver manuals
params.source: state driver handbooks

params.name: p.following_headway_wet
params.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a wet surface or in rain: the two-second rule lengthened by a second
params.source: state driver handbooks

params.name: p.following_headway_ice
params.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on an icy or snow-covered surface: the tripled following time driver manuals advise
params.source: state driver handbooks

params.name: p.following_decel_dry
params.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
params.source: AASHTO Green Book; tyre-road friction tables

params.name: p.following_decel_wet
params.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
params.source: AASHTO Green Book; tyre-road friction tables

params.name: p.following_decel_ice
params.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
params.source: tyre-road friction tables

params.name: p.truck_space_open_time
params.convention: the time a following heavy vehicle needs to open a space behind a leader that has come ahead of it, easing off by a few miles per hour: about 150 m at a closing speed near 5 m/s
params.source: heavy-vehicle following practice; commercial driver manuals

params.name: p.door_swing_reach
params.convention: lateral reach of an open passenger-car side door beyond the vehicle body (a front door opens about 0.9 to 1.1 m)
params.source: vehicle door-opening dimensions; dooring-zone guidance

params.name: p.traffic_side_door_max_open
params.convention: the longest time a traffic-side door stays open for immediate loading or unloading: a passenger pick-up or drop-off dwell at the curb
params.source: curbside passenger-loading dwell studies

params.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
params.source: heading tolerance of road-geometry alignment; lane-change heading angles

params.name: p.meeting_horizon
params.convention: the time ahead within which two vehicles closing head-on on a narrow two-way road count as meeting, so that each keeps to its half: the decision-and-steering time of a driver adjusting lateral position
params.source: AASHTO decision sight distance (avoidance manoeuvre times)

params.name: p.lateral_position_tolerance
params.convention: the lateral margin within which a vehicle body counts as at a line or an edge: lane-keeping variability of a driven vehicle plus the source's position error
params.source: lane-keeping lateral deviation studies

params.name: p.left_lane_move_over_time
params.convention: the time a driver needs, once a faster vehicle closes from behind, to check the mirrors, signal and move one lane to the right: a perception-reaction time, a few seconds of signal and the lane change
params.source: lane-change duration studies; driver manuals (signal at least 3 s before a lane change)

params.name: p.passing_sight_time
params.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
params.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

params.name: p.curvature_resolution
params.convention: the horizontal curvature at or below which a mapped roadway reads as straight: the curvature resolution of map centrelines (a radius of about two kilometres)
params.source: map centreline curvature resolution of the acquisition source

params.name: p.course_departure_sin_tol
params.convention: sine of the largest angle (about two degrees) between a moving vehicle's heading and its lane's designated direction at which it counts as keeping its course: lane-keeping heading wander plus the source's heading noise, below the few degrees of heading a lane change takes
params.source: lane-keeping and lane-change heading-angle measurements in naturalistic driving data

params.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
params.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
params.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance (left-turn time gap 7.5 s) plus a margin

params.name: p.same_time_arrival_window
params.convention: the largest difference between the times two vehicles reach an intersection's edge at which they count as arriving at approximately the same time: a two-second headway, within which neither can clear the conflict area before the other arrives
params.source: driver-manual two-second rule; follow-up headways of gap acceptance at uncontrolled junctions (Highway Capacity Manual)

params.name: p.yield_line_speed_max
params.convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at the place of a yield sign counts as having slowed: the speed from which a passenger car can still halt within the stop-point tolerance at a comfortable deceleration of about 4.5 m/s^2
params.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate of the stopping sight distance model

params.name: p.merge_window
params.convention: the time an entering or exiting vehicle takes, after coming onto or leaving the controlled-access highway, to complete its merge into or diverge from the highway's traffic: an acceleration or deceleration lane of about 250 m run at about 25 m/s
params.source: AASHTO Green Book acceleration and deceleration lane lengths

params.name: p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach
params.convention: centre distance within which an emergency or enforcement vehicle closing on a road user with its warning lamps flashing is in immediate approach: about five seconds of travel at an urban response speed of 20 m/s, the time a driver needs to perceive the lamps and begin to clear the way
params.source: driver-response studies of emergency-vehicle encounters (perception-reaction time plus lane-change time)

params.name: p.emergency_pullover_window
params.convention: the longest time from the onset of an emergency vehicle's immediate approach until a driver has moved to the right-hand edge: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one or two lane changes of about 4 s each
params.source: AASHTO perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

params.name: p.pullover_edge_gap
params.convention: the gap between a vehicle body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which a vehicle pulled over to clear the way counts as as close to the edge as it can be placed: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car (about 0.3 m) plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin
params.source: curb-parking clearance conventions of municipal codes and driver manuals

params.name: p.driver_reaction_time
params.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
params.source: Johansson and Rumar brake-reaction studies; AASHTO Green Book

params.name: p.curve_lateral_accel_max
params.convention: the lateral acceleration a passenger vehicle sustains on a curve within comfortable side friction on a dry or wet paved surface (about 0.3 g)
params.source: AASHTO Green Book side-friction factors for horizontal curves

params.name: p.lane_keeping_heading_error
params.convention: the sine of the heading error (about 1.7 degrees) that a driver's lane keeping leaves uncorrected, so that the vehicle drifts laterally at that fraction of its speed
params.source: lane-keeping and time-to-line-crossing studies (Godthelp)

params.name: p.lane_departure_time_min
params.convention: the shortest time to line crossing a driver tolerates before correcting its lateral drift: the warning threshold of lane-departure warning systems
params.source: ISO 17361 lane departure warning systems

params.name: p.low_beam_sight_reach
params.convention: the distance ahead a passenger-car low beam lights the road in darkness enough to see an obstacle
params.source: UNECE R112 / SAE J1383 low-beam photometry

params.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
params.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
params.source: emergency warning-light conspicuity studies; move-over law guidance

params.name: p.speed_decrease_decel_min
params.convention: the longitudinal deceleration at or beyond which a sampled acceleration counts as a decrease of speed rather than noise or rolling resistance: the acceleration resolution of the source
params.source: vehicle-state estimation noise of the acquisition standard

params.name: p.emergency_pass_clearance
params.convention: the gap between bodies a driver keeps while passing alongside an emergency or enforcement vehicle: a lateral passing clearance of about half a lane's free width, leaving room for its crew and doors
params.source: lateral passing-clearance conventions of driver manuals and move-over guidance

params.name: p.emergency_lane_change_window
params.convention: the time from the onset of an approach to an emergency or enforcement vehicle until a driver has moved one lane over: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one lane change of about 4 s
params.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

params.name: p.rider_evasive_decel
params.convention: the longitudinal deceleration of a bicycle or scooter rider beyond which its braking counts as an evasive reaction to another road user rather than ordinary speed control: about 0.2 g, above comfortable bicycle braking
params.source: bicycle braking studies; traffic-conflict technique

params.name: p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap
params.convention: the lateral clearance between the body of a passing motor vehicle and a bicyclist's: the bicyclist's operating-space sway beyond its body width, about one metre of free space beside it
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space)

params.name: p.vehicle_evasive_decel
params.convention: the longitudinal deceleration of a motor vehicle at or beyond which its braking counts as an evasive reaction to another road user rather than ordinary speed control: about 0.4 g, above the comfortable deceleration of about 3.4 m/s^2
params.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate; traffic-conflict studies of evasive braking

params.name: p.pedestrian_near_reach
params.convention: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a place, a region or a vehicle within which the pedestrian is near it: about two walking strides plus a curb step
params.source: pedestrian stride length (about 0.75 m) and curb heights (FHWA pedestrian facility guidance)

params.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a pedestrian signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
params.source: MUTCD section 4E.08 (pedestrian signal heads placed at the far end of the crossing, in the pedestrian's line of sight)

params.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
params.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
params.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths

params.name: p.pedestrian_clearing_speed_min
params.convention: the speed below which a pedestrian still on the roadway counts as lingering rather than proceeding to a place of safety: about half the 3.0 ft/s (0.9 m/s) walking speed to which pedestrian clearance intervals are timed for slower pedestrians
params.source: MUTCD section 4E.06 pedestrian clearance walking speeds (3.5 ft/s, 3.0 ft/s for slower pedestrians)

params.name: p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance
params.convention: the lateral margin within which a pedestrian's reference point counts as on a line that divides a region or a way: half a pedestrian's shoulder breadth plus the source's position error for a pedestrian
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual pedestrian body ellipse (about 0.6 m shoulder breadth) and pedestrian tracking position error

params.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
params.source: MUTCD signal head placement (Part 4D) and pedestrian heading variability

params.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
params.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
params.source: MUTCD far-side signal head placement (Part 4D) and urban intersection widths

params.name: p.lane_opposed_direction_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) off exactly opposed at which the designated directions of two mapped lanes of one way count as opposite directions of travel: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way
params.source: map lane-direction tolerance, matching the catalogue's tolerance for opposed vehicle headings (p.oncoming_heading_cos)

params.name: p.cross_direction_sin_min
params.convention: sine of the smallest angle (thirty degrees) by which a way's designated direction lies to one side of an approach's designated direction for that way's traffic to count as flowing to that side: the legs of a junction meet at larger angles, and map direction noise is far smaller
params.source: intersection design guidance limiting the skew of junction legs

params.name: p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) between the designated directions of two mapped lanes entering one intersection at which they count as lanes of the same approach carrying traffic the same way: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way, far below the angle between the legs of a junction
params.source: map lane-direction noise; mirrors p.lane_opposed_direction_cos proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_8a_o2

params.name: p.crest_near_reach
params.convention: the ground distance from a road user's body to a crest within which the road user is on the approach to or near the crest: the length of a crest vertical curve over which forward sight is restricted, about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance and crest vertical curve design

params.name: p.sudden_decel_min
params.convention: the longitudinal deceleration beyond which a decrease of speed counts as sudden: the comfortable deceleration most drivers use when braking for an expected stop
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, deceleration rate for stopping sight distance (3.4 m/s^2)

params.name: p.rear_signal_reach
params.convention: the gap between bodies within which a following vehicle in the same lane is immediately to the rear of a vehicle: two seconds of headway at an urban speed of about 15 m/s
params.source: two-second following rule of driver manuals

params.name: p.stop_signal_lead_window
params.convention: the time behind the onset of a halt or a sudden deceleration within which a stop or slow signal shown counts as given first for it: two perception-reaction times of an alert following driver
params.source: AASHTO perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected cue (about 1.5 s)

params.name: p.free_passage_width
params.convention: the free lateral width one passing vehicle needs beside a standing vehicle: the width of a design passenger or single-unit vehicle with its lateral clearance, about a narrow traffic lane
params.source: AASHTO design vehicle widths and lane widths (Green Book)

params.name: p.edge_standing_gap
params.convention: the gap between a standing vehicle's body and the curb or roadway edge within which the vehicle counts as standing at that edge: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked vehicle plus the source's position error
params.source: Uniform Vehicle Code parallel-parking curb clearance (18 inches) and source position error

params.name: p.commercial_loading_max_halt
params.convention: the longest halt of a commercial vehicle counted as expeditious loading or unloading of goods or passengers: the thirty-minute limit common to commercial loading zones
params.source: municipal commercial loading zone time limits

params.name: p.zone_entry_wait_reach
params.convention: the ground distance from a halted vehicle's body to a curb zone within which the vehicle counts as waiting to enter the zone: about one design passenger-car length plus the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design vehicle dimensions; HCM queue spacing

params.name: p.grade_resolution
params.convention: the longitudinal slope at or below which a roadway reads as level: the grade resolution of map elevation profiles
params.source: HD-map elevation profile accuracy specifications

params.name: p.steer_angle_resolution
params.convention: the front-wheel steering angle at or below which a parked vehicle's wheels read as straight: the steering-angle sensor resolution plus the play of a parked vehicle's wheels
params.source: steering-angle sensor specifications (SAE J670 vehicle dynamics terminology)

params.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
params.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
params.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

params.name: p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos
params.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two road users standing or moving side by side count as travelling the same way: the heading spread of vehicles queued in adjacent lanes
params.source: lane-change and queue heading variability in naturalistic driving data

params.name: p.curve_approach_reach
params.convention: the distance a road user travels ahead within which a bend it reaches counts as one it is approaching: about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h, the distance over which a driver must already be slowing for the bend
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance and horizontal curve warning placement (MUTCD Table 2C-4)

params.name: p.narrow_lane_width
params.convention: the lane width at or below which a highway's lane counts as narrow: below the 3.3 to 3.6 m design lane width at which a passenger car and a truck meet with comfortable lateral clearance
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, lane width

params.name: p.impeding_speed_margin
params.convention: the amount by which a vehicle's speed below the posted maximum of its way holds back the traffic immediately behind it: about ten miles per hour, the differential at which slow-vehicle turnout and keep-right practice treats a vehicle as slow-moving
params.source: FHWA and state slow-moving-vehicle turnout practice

params.name: p.bicycle_keep_right_gap
params.convention: the gap between a bicycle or scooter rider's body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which the rider counts as riding as near to the right side as practicable: the shy distance a bicyclist keeps from a curb or edge plus the sway of its operating space and the source's position error
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space and shy distance)

params.name: p.nearby_traffic_reach
params.convention: the gap between bodies within which another road user counts as nearby traffic: two seconds of headway at an urban speed of about 15 m/s
params.source: two-second following rule of driver manuals

params.name: p.commensurate_speed_margin
params.convention: the amount by which the speed of nearby traffic travelling the same way may exceed a rider's speed with the rider still counted as keeping pace with it: about five miles per hour, the speed differential within which road users travel as one stream
params.source: speed-study practice (5 mph speed bins, Highway Capacity Manual platoon definitions)

params.name: p.right_side_impede_reach
params.convention: the gap between a rider's body and an object or road user on its right within which that object impedes the rider's access to the right side of the roadway: about three seconds of travel at a bicyclist's cruising speed of 5 m/s, the distance within which a rider must steer around it
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist speed and reaction distance)

params.name: p.shared_lane_min_width
params.convention: the lane width below which a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot travel safely side by side within the lane: 14 ft, the wide outside lane width of bicycle facility guidance
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities; MUTCD shared-lane guidance

params.name: p.abreast_gap_max
params.convention: the gap between the bodies of two riders side by side within which they ride abreast in one row: the handlebar-to-handlebar spacing of a group riding side by side plus the source's position error
params.source: group-riding practice and bicyclist operating space (AASHTO)
